clue.text: Thoroughly awful, storing jousting equipment in stable

parts.note: well means thoroughly, as in 'well beaten'

indicators.note: to store something is to hold it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: bad means awful
a lance is the long spear used in jousting

explanation.surface: A grumble that a horrible stable has jousting gear piled inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like the noun for a horse's home, but it is an adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-balanced person or structure is steady and sensible, a synonym of stable as an adjective.

clue.text: Exult in minor role with show

parts.note: a walk-on is a small non-speaking part in a play
to air something is to show it publicly

explanation.surface: Someone delighted to have a bit part in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on air is an idiom for feeling elated, so it means to rejoice or exult.

clue.text: Means of shaping bilingual articles

parts.note: one of the two languages is French, whose feminine definite article is LA
the other language is English, whose definite article is THE

explanation.surface: A description of some dual-language writing that helps form opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bilingual articles' gives one 'the' in French (LA) and one in English (THE).
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine tool that spins wood or metal so it can be cut into shape.

clue.text: Mark of Harry getting abandoned by queen

indicators.note: the queen leaves, so her letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: to badger someone is to harry or pester them
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A sign that Prince Harry has been cast off by the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince, but it is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is an emblem or distinguishing sign, so it is a mark of identity or rank.

clue.text: What may be fruitful measure introduced by untruths

indicators.note: the measure is brought into the untruths, so it goes inside them

parts.note: lies are untruths
a metre is a unit of length

explanation.surface: A cynical observation that some fruitful scheme was launched on the back of lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruitful' reads as 'productive', but these trees literally bear fruit (limes).
explanation.definitionFit: Lime trees can bear citrus fruit, so they are things that may be fruitful in the literal sense.

clue.text: Power line knocked over during sleep remains a pain in the backside

indicators.note: the power line comes during the sleep and remains, so it sits between them

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
ash is what remains after burning
P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: in a down clue, knocking something over turns it upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: RY, for railway, is a common abbreviation for a line

explanation.surface: A power line falls over while someone naps, and the aftermath is a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pain in the backside' sounds like slang for an annoyance, but here it is literal, for a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Nappy rash is skin irritation on a baby's bottom, literally a sore spot on the backside; a nappy is a diaper.

clue.text: Summon second person to accept fine

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the second word goes inside

parts.note: in Genesis, Eve was the second person created, after Adam
OK means fine

explanation.surface: An instruction to call in someone else to agree to a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second person' looks like grammar ('you'), but it is Eve, the second human in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a spirit or memory is to call it up, so the verb is a synonym of summon.

clue.text: Lay on party — it leaves things in a rotten state

definitions.text: it leaves things in a rotten state

parts.note: to lay something down is to put it
RE means on, as in 'on the subject of'
a faction is a party or group within a larger body

explanation.surface: Someone throws a party that ends with the place trashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay on party' reads as organising an event; it is three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Putrefaction is the process of decay, so it is what leaves organic matter rotten.

clue.text: Gloomy place to sleep in Paris

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the French for 'a bed', read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' tells you to read the second meaning in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere with no lights on is dark and dismal, so the adjective is a synonym of gloomy.

clue.text: Make impervious barrier with very soft covering

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft
a roof is a covering

explanation.surface: Instructions to seal something with a barrier and a gentle covering.
explanation.definitionFit: To damp-proof a wall is to treat it so moisture cannot pass, rendering it impervious.

clue.text: Manipulates signs of credit? I don't believe it!

parts.note: to fiddle accounts is to manipulate them
ticks are marks of approval, and 'on tick' means on credit

explanation.surface: Someone cooks the books and the observer exclaims in disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an old-fashioned exclamation of disbelief or annoyance, like 'nonsense!'

clue.text: Disastrous vote-loser for one of two vote-winners

indicators.note: a disastrous thing is wrecked, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A calamitous election loser is set against two winners.
explanation.walkthrough: There were two Roosevelt presidents, Theodore and Franklin, both winners at the ballot box.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt won US presidential elections, so the surname fits either of two winners.

clue.text: Unknown competitors, not holding onto lead, accept defeat

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic unknown

indicators.note: the word loses its lead, its first letter

parts.note: the field is everyone competing in a race

explanation.surface: Unknown runners fall behind the leader and give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give in or surrender, which is conceding defeat.

clue.text: Explosive story about strike before 1st of May

indicators.note: the story goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: a fable is a story
to lam is to strike or thrash

indicators.note: takes the first letter of May

explanation.surface: A sensational tale about industrial action before May Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests a walkout but means to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flammable catches fire easily, so it is liable to blow up or ignite like an explosive.

clue.text: One could perhaps catch Jerry Maguire's opening by river mouth

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river
trap is slang for mouth

explanation.surface: Film talk of Jerry Maguire's first scene set at an estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerry Maguire' looks like the film title, but Jerry is the cartoon mouse from Tom and Jerry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousetrap catches mice, and Jerry is the famous cartoon mouse, so it might catch him.

clue.text: Breaking half of beer mugs, yet making invitation

indicators.note: takes the first two of the four letters of beer
breaking things smashes them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone smashes beer mugs yet still invites people round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' sits at the front of the clue but rearranges only MUGS and YET; BE (half of beer) stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Be my guest is a phrase offering permission, so it is a polite invitation to go ahead.

clue.text: Perhaps Lucifer's rage, after switching sides

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is': Lucifer is an example of a (fallen) angel

indicators.note: right becomes left, so an R is swapped for an L

parts.note: anger is rage

explanation.surface: Lucifer's fury after he changed allegiance in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lucifer's rage' reads as possessive, but 's is 'is'. R (right) becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer was a fallen angel in Christian tradition, so he is an example of an angel.

clue.text: Chic jacket for girl feeling desire

indicators.note: a jacket is the outside, so take the first and last letters of girl

parts.note: amorous means feeling desire

explanation.surface: A stylish jacket bought for a girl by an admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorous means stylish and alluring, a close synonym of chic.

clue.text: Posh backless dress seen around island

indicators.note: turned around, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: U means upper-class or posh

indicators.note: without its back, its last letter

parts.note: a frock is a dress

explanation.surface: A smart backless dress spotted on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backless dress' sounds like fashion, but 'backless' is an instruction to drop a letter, and 'seen around' turns the whole run, posh letter included.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Paper features in old lady's clothing not right

parts.note: ma is mother, the old lady, and 's is kept

indicators.note: not means the right is left out

parts.note: threads is slang for clothes

explanation.surface: Newspaper items about an old woman's clothes being unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A masthead is the title banner at the top of a newspaper's front page, a feature of the paper.

clue.text: Kind of music, 80 per cent country and electronic

indicators.note: four letters out of five is eighty per cent, so the last is dropped

parts.note: India is a country
E is short for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A description of music that is mostly country with some electronica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' looks like the music genre; it is the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie is a genre of alternative rock or pop, originally from independent record labels.

clue.text: One on soft drinks during bash gets the same again

indicators.note: these go during the party, so inside it

parts.note: a do is a party or bash

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece is on top of the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
TT, teetotal, means taking only soft drinks

explanation.surface: Someone on soft drinks at a party gets the same order again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same as before, used to repeat what has just been said.

clue.text: Crude oil on short rifle back in WWI campaign

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to rifle is to plunder, or pillage

indicators.note: crude means rough, unrefined, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crude oil poured on a short rifle in a First World War campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' is a verb, not a gun: PILLAGE loses its end to PILLAG, which 'back' reverses to GALLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli was the 1915-16 Allied campaign against the Ottoman Empire in the Dardanelles.

clue.text: True love found after pal finally set up

indicators.note: love comes after the pal's letter
takes the last letter of pal

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' means the letters read upwards

parts.note: to lay something is to set it down

explanation.surface: Genuine love discovered after a friend was finally framed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone loyal is faithful and steadfast, which is being true to a person or cause.

clue.text: Where pilots serve, loudly moving further on

indicators.note: moving means that letter shifts to another place in the phrase

parts.note: IN RAF: pilots serve in the Royal Air Force
F, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: Where pilots serve, noisily pressing on further.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's air arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra is Latin for below, used in texts to mean later or further on in the document.

clue.text: Number playing tie in blue getting bad name

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in the blue

parts.note: blue is the colour of the UK Conservatives, so a Tory

indicators.note: playing here means messing about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer in blue playing a tied match gets a bad reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, so it is a poor reputation or bad name.

clue.text: Mob following security measure

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a lock secures a door

explanation.surface: A crowd trailing after some new security precaution.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock is a large crowd of people, as a mob is.

clue.text: Dancing appals hosts, hosting current ball to avoid

indicators.note: to host is to have inside, so a letter goes within
dancing letters move about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Dancers horrify the hosts of a ball everyone wants to dodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance, but it is a rugby ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, a hospital pass is a pass that reaches a player just as they are about to be tackled hard.
